result:
I saved the Q3 2025 results to `/work/answer.json`. Running the same code on Q2 reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 294,266,059원 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 242 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 345,773,883원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u146@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 229 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 690,771원 |
| h. Growth from August to September | -3.5% |

Three things in the data affect the results:
- **Time zone:** Timestamps are stored in UTC (`Z`). Calculating in UTC didn't match the Q2 reference values; converting to Korean time (KST, +9 hours) matched them all. So I used KST for both the quarter boundaries and the month grouping. For example, an order at 2025-09-30T15:30Z counts as Q4 (October 1, 00:30 KST).
- **Inconsistent labels:** Segment and category names vary in case and spacing (e.g. "Enterprise ", " consumer"). I trimmed spaces and made them lowercase before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** There are 300 customer rows but only 250 unique emails. I counted customers by email (trimmed and lowercased), not by customer ID; this affects b, e and f.

STATUS: DONE
